player_0.content: New plan: My previous attempt failed because I assigned a high score (8) to "Disappointment," which is an emotion typically felt by the person who is let down (Vanessa), not the one who caused the harm and is being rejected (Felix). Felix's primary emotional state is the crushing realization of total loss and the inability to fix his mistake, which aligns strictly with "Despair." "Relief" is impossible given the rejection, and "Vindication" is the opposite of his situation. Next time, I will strictly analyze the perspective of the specific character asked about (Felix) and assign a score of 0 to emotions that logically belong to the other character or contradict the context of being the perpetrator of a betrayal. I will focus the high intensity solely on Despair, as it is the only emotion that accurately reflects Felix's state of having lost his friend and reputation with no recourse.
